_comment: Item-level watches. Separate from src/data/tracking.json on purpose: tracked brands produce aggregate statistics (counts, medians, velocity), whereas a watch hunts individual listings and alerts on them. A brand with no comparable segment, like Chrome Hearts, belongs here rather than on the brand board, where its jewelry would corrupt the price medians.
_rules: A listing matches when it clears minPrice, its title contains at least one term from require.any (and every term from require.all, if given), and contains none from exclude. Terms are matched case-insensitively on word boundaries, so 'ring' does not match 'earring' or 'Bering'. Set enabled:false to park a watch without deleting it.
_credibility: eBay returns asking prices, not sales. A dry run on 2026-09-17 showed why seller checks matter more than price here: five-figure asks came from accounts with 0 ratings, 3 ratings, and one with -1. Every clean match came from an established seller (98.8% over 315 ratings, 100% over 1222). Thresholds were loosened from 97%/50 to 95%/20 because a legitimate seller at 96.4% over 344 ratings was being caught, but they stay strict enough to reject a $25,900 ask from a brand new account. maxPrice caps the fantasy tier and maxAlertsPerRun stops a first run flooding the channel.

watches.label: Chrome Hearts grail denim and high-ticket tops
watches.notes: Targets the tier that sells five figures: Levi's and Carhartt collabs with leather or ponyhair cross patches, the Matty Boy and Sex Records lines, city and event exclusives, and high-ticket outerwear. Scope is denim plus expensive tops only. Hoodies, tees and sweats are the standard tier and are not hunted; the $5,000 floor is what keeps them out, so it should not be lowered to chase recall. Marker vocabulary comes from Eli's own catalogue, where 140 of 256 pieces carry one of these and the rest are plain stock. Fashionphile carries no Chrome Hearts apparel at all, so eBay is the only accessible source.

watches.label: Hermès Birkin 25
watches.notes: Core cohort. Fashionphile confirms sales, so SOLD here is a real transaction. Set targetPrice to be told when one lists or drops below what you would pay.

_events: Each watch reports three events. NEW: an eligible listing appeared. PRICE DROP: a tracked listing fell to a new low by at least dropPct (default 5), so a seller raising a price and trimming it back does not count. SOLD / NO LONGER LISTED: a tracked listing left the market. Fashionphile confirms sales; eBay cannot distinguish a sale from a withdrawal, so its departures are reported as no longer listed. targetPrice marks any new listing or drop at or below it as UNDER TARGET. The first run of a new watch records standing listings silently, so a month-old listing is never announced as new.
_privacy: This repository is public, so this file is world-readable. A targetPrice here tells anyone what you are hunting and what you would pay. Keep sensitive targets out of the file or make the repository private before setting them.
